- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-1.0) or shows strong reversal, model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, especially after negative sentiment — apply smoothing or lagged correction to avoid sharp reversals.
- In cases of sustained upward trend with positive sentiment, model often fails to account for mean reversion; reduce forecast slope after 3–5 consecutive positive sentiment days.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after a spike, model often fails to anticipate — add a downward bias correction in the first 3–5 days post-spike.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed — apply a 5–10% downward adjustment for the first 7–10 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model often misjudges the direction — favor averaging recent 3–5 day sentiment to guide correction.
